headline: Achieve Real-Time 60 FPS Video Segmentation in 16.67ms on Android
summary: Mastering real-time video segmentation on Android requires precise hardware and software optimization.
details: Real-time video segmentation on Android requires achieving 60 frames per second (FPS), which translates to 16.67 milliseconds per frame. Any delay beyond this threshold results in a poor user experience.

To accomplish this, developers must optimize their AI pipeline, leveraging hardware acceleration and model compression. The CPU is inefficient for AI inference due to its sequential processing nature.

Modern Android SoCs utilize heterogeneous computing, distributing the workload across the NPU, GPU, and DSP. The NPU handles tensor operations, the GPU manages pixel manipulation, and the DSP handles low-bit-depth operations.
AICore, a system service, provides a standardized AI provider interface, enabling developers to access optimized AI models and reducing binary bloat.

headline: Ploy switches to GPT-5.6 Sol: 2.2x faster
summary: GPT-5.6 Sol outperforms Claude Opus, reducing costs by 27%
details: Ploy's AI agent now runs on GPT-5.6 Sol, OpenAI's flagship model. This switch brings 2.2x faster performance and 27% lower costs.
The new model was chosen after head-to-head testing against Claude Opus. GPT-5.6 Sol is the first model to beat Opus in Ploy's rigorous evaluations.
Migrating to GPT-5.6 Sol required significant changes to Ploy's evaluation harness and tooling. The new model uses parallel calls and batched file reads, which the previous harness didn't support.
GPT-5.6 Sol produces high-quality, modern designs but can struggle with brand adherence if not properly steered. Ploy's team worked to adapt the model to their specific needs.
